classification.difficultyReason: Identify named features of an isosceles triangle, measure its legs and base angles, and state the equal-base-angle property.

content.prompt: In the isosceles triangle to the right, $PQ=PR$.

spec.sourceRegion: Exercise 13C question 1, diagram to the right of parts a–e
spec.description: Unshaded isosceles triangle PQR with matching single leg ticks and horizontal base extended beyond R. Ordinary source blue strokes are reconstructed in house black. Geometry is deliberately calibrated to the answer evidence rather than inferred from raster scale.
spec.mathematics: PQ=PR=30 mm at the specified 40 mm bounding-box width; the interior base angles are each 67 degrees. Coordinates give QR approximately 23.443868 mm and altitude approximately 27.615146 mm. Lengths and angle values are not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only vertex labels, equal-leg ticks and the original base extension are visible; measured answers remain hidden.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Name the apex of the isosceles triangle.

answer.worked: The equal legs $PQ$ and $PR$ meet at $P$, so the apex is $P$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Name the legs and measure their lengths.

answer.worked: The marked equal sides $PQ$ and $PR$ are the legs. Measuring each with a ruler gives $PQ=PR=3\text{ cm}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Name the base of the isosceles triangle.

answer.worked: The third side, opposite the apex $P$, is $QR$, so the base is $QR$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Name the base angles and measure their sizes.

answer.worked:
The base angles are at $Q$ and $R$. Place the protractor centre at each vertex and align its baseline with $QR$ or $RQ$, respectively. Read the interior angle to the corresponding leg:
$$\begin{align*}\angle PQR&\approx67^{\circ}\\\angle PRQ&\approx67^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: What property of isosceles triangles do these angle sizes illustrate?

answer.short: The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.
answer.worked: The measured base angles $\angle PQR$ and $\angle PRQ$ are equal. This illustrates that the base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.
